jsmith.sales: FYI OrchidBank (EU-regulated) wants BYOK with HSM for a short POC. Requirements: keys must be created inside customer HSM (no export), all KMS traffic must remain in EU, rotation cadence asked for 60d (they asked whether 90d is possible), audit/usage logs streaming to their Splunk, and no Redwood storage of plaintext keys. They want pricing for Dedicated vs Private and a SOW clause for escrow-only-under-court. Any blockers?
marie.solutions: Quick clarifying q: do they require FIPS-validated modules and tamper-evidence attestation? That will affect vendor list and onboarding timeline.
tom.crypto: We support born-in-HSM flows. Vendors we've certified: AWS CloudHSM (PKCS#11), Thales Luna, and Utimaco (PKCS#11). For strict EU-only egress we need VPC peering/PrivateLink + route filters. Note: 60d rotation is fine but increases ops coordination; we recommend a 24h dual-key acceptance window to avoid outages.
emma.orchid: Confirmed: OrchidBank wants to orchestrate rotation from their side; Redwood must accept both old and new keys during a 24h transition. Also they want a SOC2 appendix and EU data residency notes in the SOW.
marie.solutions: We'll put a rotation playbook into the SOW (steps, validation, rollback, contact matrix). We also need their DR escrow policy (sealed offline escrow invoked only under legal writ). Legal needs to review exact wording.
legal-bot: Please attach proposed escrow clause. Engineering/legal will review and flag any compliance or indemnity gotchas. Also check whether 60d triggers an ops surcharge.
finance.ops: There is a one-time BYOK HSM integration fee and a monthly EU private deployment premium. Dedicated typically has lower unit cost but requires a commit; Private has higher baseline. I'll upload a pricing delta sheet by EOD.
infra-bot: Runbook created: /runbooks/sales/orchid-byok-poc-checklist (includes connectivity checks, cert guidance, and contact matrix). :white_check_mark:
marie.solutions: Share these connectivity tests with the customer's bastion team:
```bash
# from customer bastion -> Redwood proxy
curl -v --cert client.pem --key client.key https://kms-proxy.eu-west-1.redwood-internal/health
# verify TLS cert fingerprint
openssl s_client -connect kms-proxy.eu-west-1.redwood-internal:443 -servername kms.orchid.internal | openssl x509 -noout -fingerprint -sha256
```
tom.crypto: Also request PKCS#11 module checksum, HSM firmware version, supported key types (AES-256-GCM, RSA-3072, ECDSA P-384), and vendor import API docs. If they insist on no-export keys, the customer must perform the import in their HSM console or provide a PKCS#11 endpoint for remote ops.
emma.orchid: We'll upload the vendor docs and open a temporary bastion for Thursday 09:00 CET for the preflight. We'll also provide CIDR ranges and DNS names.
marie.solutions: Action items: 1) @tom.crypto produce vendor compatibility matrix + latency SLA targets. 2) @finance.ops post Dedicated vs Private price delta. 3) @legal-bot review escrow/dr clause and SOC2 appendix. 4) @emma.orchid send CIDRs, bastion window, and vendor docs.
jsmith.sales: Thanks all 44d. If preflight is green we can convert the POC to a 30-day trial and then move to Dedicated commit if they like performance and costs. :rocket:
